Priya (Finance): Heads-up — our cloud partner just pushed new committed-use pricing in eu-west1 and us-west1. Need a quick pass on how this changes unit economics for Dedicated commitments. Can infra/cost ops weigh in?
Alex (Infra): saw the update. Net effective H100 on-demand up ~12% in us-west1, reserved discount rate cut ~6 percentage points for 1y commits.
Maya (SRE): cluster health unrelated but FYI some preemptible pools are already seeing capacity pressure in eu-west1. Not great for burst fallback.
Julian (Cost Ops): running a baseline calc now. If on-demand +12% and committed discount -6pp, our blended per-GPU-hour goes up roughly 8-10% depending on utilization.
Priya (Finance): rough 📈 margin impact for Dedicated customers? We have 20% gross margin target on Dedicated SLAs currently.
Julian (Cost Ops): quick sketch: assume previous cost C0. New cost C1 ~= C0 * (1 + 0.10) (blended). So margin M drops from (P-C0)/P to (P-C1)/P. If price P is fixed, margin shrink ~ (C1-C0)/P. Example: P=2.50$/GPU-hr, C0=1.50 -> M0=40%. C1=1.65 -> M1=34% => -6pp.
Priya (Finance): thanks. That -6pp would push some SKUs below threshold. Options? raise price, absorb, or renegotiate commits.
Alex (Infra): technical levers: more aggressive batching, enable 4-bit quantization profiles for compatible models, and move low-priority traffic to cheaper zones. But each has tradeoffs (latency/QoE/regional constraints).
Sam (Product): Product risk: customers on Dedicated expect predictable latency. We can selectively recommend quantization for non-latency-critical models and offer a premium low-latency tier.
Rina (Sales): we also have a pipeline of renewals in EU this quarter — need clear messaging if price pass-through is considered. Customers will push back on sudden increases.
Maya (SRE): we should evaluate routing policy: prefer eu-west2 for burst if capacity exists; but network egress cost differs. I'll run a capacity delta map tonight.
Julian (Cost Ops): I can produce a sensitivity table for 3 scenarios (absorb, pass-through 10% price increase, selective SKU bump).
Priya (Finance): please do. Also include committed vs reserved term options (1y vs 3y) — longer terms might restore margin via deeper discounts, but we need volume confidence.
Alex (Infra): note: 3y commits are limited in some regions due to capacity procurement lead times. Ops risk needs a note.
BillingBot: Invoice update processed for account redwood-prod: new rates effective 2026-11-01.
Julian (Cost Ops): action plan: 1) I'll attach sensitivity table (by EOD) with per-GPU-hour impacts and margin delta. 2) Alex + Maya to provide feasibility of latency-cost levers. 3) Priya/Rina discuss go-to-market messaging.
Priya (Finance): perfect. If Julian posts the numbers here, we can decide whether a partial price-tier adjustment is necessary for renewals this quarter.
Alex (Infra): preliminary note: if we enable prefix caching aggressively for chat workloads we can reduce token compute by ~6-9% for certain customers — worth modeling into the sensitivity.
Julian (Cost Ops): will add cache/quantization/burst-routing columns. Expected timeline: draft by EOD, finalized by tomorrow AM.
Rina (Sales): I'll prep a short customer FAQ template in case of price changes.
Sam (Product): also flag customers with SLOs tied to latency — those get separate handling.
Priya (Finance): thanks all. Let's reconvene after Julian posts the sensitivity table. :thumbsup:
